subject: Pilot SLA routing & deployment recommendation for Quicksilver
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@quicksilver.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLA routing & deployment recommendation for Quicksilver

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Short recap and a proposed path so we can align on an executable pilot:

Call recap:
- Primary goal: integrate search & checkout features with sub-100ms p95 for short user interactions (query -> suggestion).
- Current traffic shape: steady baseline during business hours with intermittent spikes from marketing pushes and nightly batch re-ranks (you mentioned a ~90s window of concentrated traffic).
- Security: Quicksilver needs SOC2 attestation review and an option for VPC/private deployment later in the roadmap.

Preliminary numbers / asks from our side:
- Can you confirm expected average request payload (tokens) and whether prompts include long historical context?
- Can you share an anonymized 24h QPS sample if possible (we asked for this on the call) — will use it to size batchers and recommend throughput.

Recommended pilot approach (proposal):
- Phase A (2-week pilot): run on Redwood Hosted API to get telemetry fast. Hosted gives us immediate telemetry (p95, p99, token cost) and lets us validate real-world latency/quantization tradeoffs.
- Phase B (if sustained p95 < 120ms at target QPS) continue Hosted for production; if p95 degrades or predictable peak windows exceed our routing policy thresholds, upgrade to Dedicated capacity for production traffic.
- For your big marketing spikes we propose an automated routing policy: normal traffic -> Hosted; spikes above X qps -> route to a Dedicated burst pool (reserved for 8h windows).

Attachments: I attached a quick template for load profiles to fill out (qs-pilot-load-profiles.xlsx) and a short routing proposal (redwood-routing-proposal.pdf).

Immediate next steps:
1) Evan/Priya: attach the 24h anonymized QPS sample and a typical payload example.
2) Quicksilver: nominate an internal technical point-of-contact to run the pilot checklist.
3) We will provision a Hosted test key and a short burst Dedicated estimate to show cost delta for your spikes.

If you prefer to go straight to Dedicated for the pilot (you mentioned wanting strict p95 guarantees), say so and we’ll supply a Dedicated pilot quote and SLA terms.

Thanks — I’ll block time for a 30-minute kick-off once we have the QPS sample.

Jonas Weber

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications and I attached the 24h sample as promised.

Answers / context:
- Average payload: ~80 tokens per request (mostly short queries). Context window rarely exceeds 256 tokens (we strip long histories at the UI).
- 24h sample: baseline ~120 qps during peak business hours, with three spike events: 1) marketing email — +480 qps for ~6 minutes, 2) nightly catalog sync causing re-rank burst ~200 qps for ~12 minutes, 3) European morning overlap boosting baseline by ~30%.
- Our product team is sensitive to p95 for query suggestions — target is <100ms p95; if the pilot suggests consistent p95 > 150ms we will push for Dedicated.

Security note: SOC2 packets are in procurement; Priya will send the secure link for the compliance docs later today. We prefer Hosted for speed of pilot, but want clarity on what Dedicated buys us (predicted p95 reduction and cost delta).

Evan Brooks

Evan / Priya — appreciate the sample. Quick tech checklist so we size correctly and avoid surprises during the pilot:

Technical clarifications (please reply inline where possible):
- Payload distribution: can you split the sample by endpoint (query vs checkout vs re-rank)? We need separate profiles because re-ranks are token-heavy and affect KV cache behavior.
- Token length p95: you said ~80 tokens average — what is p95 token length?
- Latency tolerance for batch vs single-token paths: are you willing to accept slightly higher tail latency for re-ranks (they are not user-blocking) if it reduces unit cost?
- Authentication: will you use API keys initially or require mTLS from day 1? This impacts Hosted onboarding timeline.

Initial technical recommendation based on what you sent:
- Pilot: Run on Hosted API with the following runtime settings: 1) continuous small batching up to 16 requests or 2s, 2) prefix KV cache enabled for repeated suggestion patterns, 3) token quantization profile Q2 for cost/latency balance.
- Routing policy: configure an automated spike rule at 350 qps that triggers a burst Dedicated pool for 6–8 minutes. That lets us keep steady traffic on Hosted and absorb short marketing spikes without experiencing cold-start variability.
- If you need firm p95 SLAs below 100ms across sustained windows (10+ minutes), plan to move production to Dedicated capacity with pinned model weights and reserved throughput.

Attachments: small checklist for the pilot harness and an example traffic-split config (attached inline).

Proposed immediate next step: a 45-minute kickoff this Thursday to validate sample splits and agree on the spike threshold (I can run through the routing playbook).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

Evan / Priya — thanks for the quick responses and the sample. Finalizing a suggested execution plan below so procurement and engineering can action this week.

Recommended execution (concise):
1) Pilot mode (2 weeks): Hosted API
   - We’ll provision a test API key, set continuous batching up to 16 / 2s, enable prefix KV cache, and apply quantization Q2.
   - Routing: spike trigger at 350 qps -> temporary Dedicated burst pool (we estimate a 6–8 minute reserve during spikes).
   - Success criteria: sustained p95 <= 120ms for query endpoint under baseline; no more than one spike-induced p95 breach per pilot week.

2) Contingency: If pilot shows p95 > 150ms for queries under baseline traffic, we provision a short Dedicated run (48–72 hours) to benchmark pinned-weight performance and give you firm p95 predictions for production.

3) Compliance / procurement:
   - Priya: please share the SOC2 review link and any procurement timelines; we’ll supply the Dedicated pilot quote and contract redlines within 48 hours.

4) Kickoff: proposed Thursday 2027-04-01 10:00 AM PT (45 minutes) — agenda: sample split, spike threshold, test key handoff. Confirm if that works and we’ll calendar invite.

I’ll attach the Dedicated cost delta and a one-page SLA comparison in the kickoff doc ahead of the meeting.

If you want to skip Hosted and run the initial pilot on Dedicated, we can do that, but it will add setup time (provisioning + contract) — tradeoff: faster p95 certainty vs slower telemetry.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Jonas Weber
